facts_from_discussion: The court found no material facts to be in genuine dispute.
Petitioner does not dispute that he received the SSDI benefits during 2022.

Petitioner did not challenge the mechanics of respondent's computation of the includible amount; his argument is that the 2022 benefits should be excluded because he was obliged to repay, and did repay, them to SSA.
Petitioner made no repayment of Social Security benefits to SSA during 2022; his repayments were made during 2023 and 2024.
The SSDI benefits were paid under title II of the Social Security Act.

Petitioner applied for the benefits and SSA issued him a letter affirming his entitlement to them; it was not until 2023 that SSA reversed its decision after learning that he had been employed during 2022.
Petitioner argued that the 2022 benefits were tantamount to loan proceeds and relied on the claim of right doctrine; he also argued for an offset or loss on account of his 2023 and 2024 repayments.
2022 is the only year before the court.
